$description: derate design tokens. Three layers: primitives (ramps and scales), semantic (roles; the CSS names the UI already uses), component (parts). A $value that is an object keyed light/dark/high-contrast differs per theme; everything else is theme-invariant. Build: cd .omp && npm run tokens:build.

color.$description: Primitive ramps. Every step is a value the UI already paints (the warm neutrals are derate's whole surface and ink system); steps are ordered by lightness and named on a 50-grid with intermediates where two existing values sit close together. Near-duplicate pairs (ΔE < 3: stone.900/925, stone.650/700, stone.150/200) are kept distinct on purpose -- the migration is pixel-exact -- and are candidates for a later merge, recorded in AUDIT.md.

100.$description: stone 100: panel light; ink, on-fill, on-signal dark

400.$description: blue 400: info-solid dark (OKLCH midpoint of 300 and 500)

500.$description: blue 500: flow light, 4.22:1 -- a mark, not text

600.$description: blue 600: info light, 5.19:1 on panel -- the text-grade step of the flow hue

alpha.$description: Translucent colours. Composited over the surface before contrast is measured.

white-94.$description: initials on a publisher accent plate

1.$description: publisher avatar hue 1; identity, never status; theme-invariant

2.$description: publisher avatar hue 2; identity, never status; theme-invariant

3.$description: publisher avatar hue 3; identity, never status; theme-invariant

4.$description: publisher avatar hue 4; identity, never status; theme-invariant

5.$description: publisher avatar hue 5; identity, never status; theme-invariant

6.$description: publisher avatar hue 6; identity, never status; theme-invariant

7.$description: publisher avatar hue 7; identity, never status; theme-invariant

8.$description: publisher avatar hue 8; identity, never status; theme-invariant

9.$description: publisher avatar hue 9; identity, never status; theme-invariant

10.$description: publisher avatar hue 10; identity, never status; theme-invariant

space.$description: Spacing, named by its px value. Emitted directly as --space-<px>; there is no second vocabulary.

raised-light.$description: dialog, popover on the light page

raised-dark.$description: dialog, popover on the dark page

raised-high-contrast.$description: a hard outline: shadows do not read at high contrast

standard.$description: the house curve: fast out, soft landing

default.$description: browser default, used by the legacy transitions

semantic.$description: Roles. Reference primitives only. The CSS custom property is the last path segment, unchanged from the names derate's components already use.

panel-raised.$description: dialog, popover. The ramp inverts as a whole in dark so "raised" still means lighter-than-page.

ink-secondary.$description: text one step quieter than ink, still ≥ 7:1 on panel

ink-muted.$description: labels, units. 5.84:1 light -- #6E6A62 measured 4.44 and failed AA on 12px text

rule.$description: hairlines. 1.47:1: decorative, excluded from the contrast gate

edge.$description: boundaries that must be PERCEIVABLE: control borders and meter-track keylines. 3.54:1 light, 3.85:1 dark

fill.$description: the inverted plate, distinct from text ink -- a selection outline in ink on a fill plate was 1.00:1

select-on-panel.$description: selection drawn outside a plate, against the page (= ink)

select-on-fill.$description: selection drawn inside a plate (= on-fill)

live.$description: healthy, as text on panel. 5.08:1 light

warn.$description: degraded, as text on panel. 5.03:1 light -- #8A6318 measured 4.47

fault.$description: failed, as text on panel. 6.02:1 light

info.$description: informational, as text on panel. The flow hue one step darker so it clears 4.5:1

live-solid.$description: healthy, as a fill or dot

warn-solid.$description: degraded, as a fill or dot. 2.67:1 on the light page: a dot, never a surface for text

fault-solid.$description: failed, as a fill or dot

info-solid.$description: informational, as a fill or dot

on-signal.$description: marks drawn on a -solid fill; 3:1 is the bar, these are not text surfaces

flow.$description: a request in flight. An accent, not a grey: it is a real measured event

stream.$description: output tokens leaving, streamed. A filled mark: 4.04:1 light clears SC 1.4.11

batch.$description: output tokens leaving, buffered. Not drawn since 2026-11-18: /cluster's response blocks are --stream and say buffered vs streamed by block width alone. Kept because tabs/chat/tags.ts picks its tag hues clear of it and DESIGN.md's traffic row names it

accent.$description: the default publisher accent (= flow). ModelCard overrides --accent inline per publisher: the one token set at runtime, from data

tag-1.$description: chat turn identity 1. USE ORDER, NOT SPECTRUM: blue, magenta, teal, violet so the two-model case is the 100° pair. Nothing within 42° of a status hue.

hover.$description: hover wash. Derived from --ink at paint time, so one expression serves light and dark

focus-ring.$description: alias of focus for component tokens

limit.$description: a rate limit applied to a served name (wiring editor `limit` sockets and wires). Magenta: 42deg+ from every status hue

size-mono-readout-xl.$description: mono partner of readout-xl, one notch tighter: Plex Mono renders optically larger

size-mono-body.$description: mono partner of body; setup commands

size-body-sm.$description: sans at mono-body size: setup facts

focus-ring-width.$description: focus ring stroke; 3px at high contrast

component.$description: Per-component tokens. Reference semantics only; CSS name --<component>-<part>.

$extensions.derate.pinned: cards are flat in every theme; shadow.none has no semantic role to sit behind

ink.$description: theme-invariant: the QR tile is pinned light by design so a phone camera reads it in both themes

$extensions.derate.pinned: the QR tile is pinned light in every theme so a phone camera reads it; see setup.css .setup-qr

toast.$description: specified, not built: inline status is the default

graph.$description: the /cluster wiring editor: block chrome, the five socket/wire types, issue colours

fault.$description: a wire or block an issue names as broken

warn.$description: a wire or block worth a look
